evals.prompt: Can you audit our iOS app's Mapbox integration? We're on MapboxMaps 11.20 with UIKit and a custom style. In MapScreenViewController.viewDidLoad we have `_ = mapView.mapboxMap.onStyleLoaded.observe { [weak self] _ in self?.addStoreLayers() }`, and the store layers sometimes don't show up. We also call `_ = mapView.camera.ease(to: camera, duration: 0.5)` in a few places.
expectations: Identifies the dropped AnyCancelable from onStyleLoaded.observe as the cause: the token cancels the subscription when released, so the observer never fires (MAPSIOS-B-HYGIENE-1)
Recommends storing the token (for example in a Set<AnyCancelable> with .store(in:)) for as long as the observer should live
Does not flag the discarded Cancelable from camera.ease, since that plain Cancelable doesn't cancel when released
Reports findings in the output schema with File:line, the matching ID, confidence and false-positive risk
Does not recommend switching to Mapbox Standard, since the app uses a custom style

evals.prompt: Audit this Android tap handler in our Maps SDK 11.22 app (custom style, View system): `mapView.gestures.addOnMapClickListener { point -> mapboxMap.queryRenderedFeatures(RenderedQueryGeometry(mapboxMap.pixelForCoordinate(point)), RenderedQueryOptions(listOf("stores"), null)) { r -> val f = r.value?.firstOrNull(); if (f != null) select(f) else clearSelection() }; true }`. select() rewrites the stores GeoJsonSource with a selected=true property.
expectations: Recommends Featureset Interactions: ClickInteraction.layer("stores") registered with mapboxMap.addInteraction (MAPS-A1.5)
Points out the empty-map branch (clearSelection) needs its own ClickInteraction { ctx -> } (MAPS-A1.6), or it is lost in the migration
Flags the source rewrite for selection as MAPS-B-STYLE-3 and recommends setFeatureState with a featureState expression (MAPS-A2.1/A2.2)
Mentions the feature-state preconditions: stable feature ids (promoteId or generateId) and paint properties only
Does not recommend Standard-only interactions or switching to Standard

evals.prompt: We use Mapbox Navigation SDK 3.24 on Android. Our RouteProgressObserver computes remaining distance by summing leg annotation distances from the current index on every update, and our TripFragment calls mapboxNavigation.registerRouteProgressObserver { progress -> updateEta(progress) } in onViewCreated. Is there anything wrong here?
expectations: Flags the manual remaining-distance computation as NAV-NRO-1 and recommends routeProgress.distanceRemaining (or the leg and step progress fields)
Flags the inline-lambda observer as NAV-MEMORY-3: it can't be unregistered, and registering in onViewCreated accumulates observers across view recreation
Recommends keeping a reference to the observer and unregistering it in the matching teardown
Cites the NAV IDs and gives confidence and false-positive risk for each finding

evals.prompt: Review our Android search screen. We use Search SDK 2.30 with SearchEngine. The EditText's text watcher calls searchEngine.search(text, SearchOptions(), callback) on every change, and when the user taps a suggestion we read suggestion.coordinate and drop a marker there.
expectations: Flags searching on every keystroke without a debounce (SEARCH-B-REQUEST-1) and recommends SearchOptions.requestDebounce or a UI-layer debounce, but not both
Flags using the suggestion's coordinate without select as SEARCH-B-FLOW-1: the field is restricted and usually null, and the resolved result comes from select
Recommends calling searchEngine.select(suggestion, ...) and using the SearchResult coordinate
Uses IDs that exist in the Search reference, such as SEARCH-B-FLOW-1 and SEARCH-B-REQUEST-1 for findings and SEARCH-P3 / SEARCH-P4 for the checks, rather than invented ones

evals.prompt: Please do a full audit of our Android delivery app's Mapbox setup. It uses Navigation SDK 3.25 and Maps SDK 11.25. Don't change any code yet.
expectations: Plans to confirm the SDK versions from the Gradle files (or version catalog) and picks both the navigation-android and maps-android references
Lays out the inventory checks (NAV-P1, MAPS-P1) first, then the remaining checks one at a time, skipping ones that don't apply with a reason
Doesn't change code, since the audit is read-only and the developer asked for no changes
Describes a report with a summary, findings grouped by check in priority order using the output schema, a checked-not-flagged section and [VERIFY WITH MAPBOX] items

evals.prompt: Our Android Maps SDK 11.20 app has no mapView.onStart()/onStop()/onDestroy() calls anywhere and no mapView.lifecycle reference. We create MapView with the default MapInitOptions. Is our MapView lifecycle broken?
expectations: Explains the lifecycle plugin is in MapInitOptions.defaultPluginList and is installed by default, so no manual calls are needed
Concludes this is the recommended integration (MAPS-B-HYGIENE-1 case D), a pass, not a bug
Warns against inferring the plugin is missing from the absence of a mapView.lifecycle call site
Mentions what would still be a finding, such as a MapView held in a ViewModel, singleton or DI singleton, or teardown in onDestroyView that calls into the map
